content:
The image shows young banana fingers on a bunch. Key observations:

- **Affected part**: Banana fruit tips (distal/perianth end of each finger)
- **Visual features**: Dark blackening and shriveling concentrated at the tips of the banana fingers, starting from the perianth (flower end). The tips appear dry, shrunken, and have a powdery/ashy dark coloration — resembling ash at the end of a cigar.
- The rest of the fruit body remains green and apparently healthy, with the damage confined to the blossom-end tips.

**Matching against classes:**
- **Cigar End Rot** perfectly matches: "infection spreads from the perianth to the fingers, causing blackening of the skin, shrinkage and folding of tissues, with affected tissues corrugated and covered with powdery grey conidia resembling ash on a cigar end." The visual appearance of dark, dried, shrunken tips is the hallmark of this disease.
- Anthracnose causes sunken black lesions on the fruit body, not confined to tips.
- Other classes affect leaves or the whole plant, not fruit tips in this pattern.
